title: Massapootupaug
summary: Massapootupaug is a western Southampton placename connected with a 1662 Shinnecock conveyance boundary near Niamack, Canoe Place, and the old gutt.
why_this_matters: A 1662 land deed transferring Shinnecock territory to Captain Topping used the Algonquian name Massapootupaug to mark the westernmost boundary of the south side. Examining these early colonial transactions reveals how indigenous leaders actively negotiated their borders, while also showing how Native place names were permanently inscribed into the legal foundation of Long Island's towns.
introduction_content: Massapootupaug is associated with a locality in the western part of Southampton town.
translation_content:
The recorded variant is Masspootupaug. Massapootupaug is interpreted as a great bay or cove with a narrow inlet from a river or sea, while noting that an earlier interpretation as great boggy meadow was later reconsidered.

Why Place Names Matter

“Personal names and place names are like baskets that hold a piece of history. They connect to ancient histories that often go back to the origin stories of the First Nation who holds them.”

— First Nations Education Steering Committee and First Nations Schools Association, BC First Peoples 12 Teacher Resource Guide (2022), Printed p. 152; PDF page 152, Place Names section
whereintheworld_content: Existing polygon retained. The shape represents a general western Southampton / south-side location associated with Niamack, Canoe Place, and the old gutt; it should not be treated as an exact deed boundary.
